name: Distill — Activation Atlas
oneLine: Peer-reviewed ML article whose hero is a zoomable atlas of a CNN's learned features; rigorous academic shell, dazzling figures.

palette.note: Article page; atlas sits on a #EFEFEF panel
Body is black at 80% opacity; secondary text steps down via 60/50/30% black
Orange for selected layer (MIXED4D), zoom buttons, and diagram points/arrows
15% blue tint behind classifier result rows ('grey whale 91.0%')
15% green tint for the altered-prediction row ('great white shark 66.7%')

type.note: Title ~50px weight 700, tight -1% tracking, two lines; H2 'Introduction' ~36px bold with a hairline rule below
16.96px regular, ~1.8 line-height, 700px column; citations as small blue bracketed [1, 2, 3]
9-13px for UI: uppercase layer names MIXED3A..MIXED5B in gray, orange when active; figure captions 13px gray

layout: Classic Distill grid: 700px text column centered, while figures break out to a wider ~1100px or full 1440px (atlas spans edge to edge under the abstract).
Atlas figure is a mini app: 170px left rail of layer thumbnails, central tiled-image canvas, floating top-right control card with minimap.
Four-up explanatory diagrams in a row (axes, plane, manifold, grid) with 13px captions beneath, each linking to prior work.
motion: (inferred) Pan/zoom on the atlas is smooth and continuous, with tiles resolving to higher-resolution feature visualizations as you zoom (tiled canvas, 11 canvases).
(inferred) Switching layers in the left rail crossfades the atlas; hover tooltips show the top attributed classes per cell.
Static prose otherwise: motion is reserved entirely for the figures, giving them maximal punch.
interactions: Zoomable, pannable atlas with home/+/- buttons, minimap, and checkboxes for attribution labels, tooltips, and scroll-to-zoom.
Layer selector rail with orange active state and silhouette thumbnails.
Adversarial patch demo: paste a baseball onto a whale image and watch the classifier's top-1 flip.
steal: Latent-space explorer: a full-bleed zoomable atlas of our telemetry windows (tiles = representative signal snippets) with a minimap card in the top-right.
Model-layer rail: left column of thumbnails for encoder layers / model variants with a single accent active state, reused in our model-comparison section.
Prediction rows: tinted result bars ('nominal 91.0%' vs 'anomaly 66.7%') in before/after pairs for our failure-case gallery.
leave: Default checkboxes and gray 'more options' button feel like research-tool chrome; our controls need custom, fully-stated components.
Bright saturated header plus white academic body is credible but not cinematic; keep the rigor (citations, author block) but not the paper look.
